title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Analysis situs, third version (June 1986). This is Grothendieck's axiomatic attempt at a 'tame topology' (the topologie modérée of the Esquisse, §5). Spaces are replaced by 'figures', which are stratified objects. A figure F has a poset of strata F~ = I, ordered by the face/specialisation relation. There is an ambient M (a set of strata or figures) with a lattice Σ_M of 'supports'. Each object Z has a support supp Z and a complementary 'cosupport' cosupp Z. The relation Z ∥ X ('Z is disjoint from X') holds iff Z lies in cosupp X.

The previous page showed by a planar example that this support lattice is neither distributive nor even modular. Its Scholium: the support formalism is fine provided one does not compare supports of strata and of compatible figures carelessly.

This page states the intuition to be made precise. Elements of I should behave like 'open strata', and P(I) should be identifiable with a family of supports, namely unions of open strata.

To give an intrinsic meaning to 'X minus its boundary' for a stratum X, Grothendieck defines X° = supp_M X ∩ cosupp_M ∂X (a subset of M). Here ∂X = {Y in M | Y < X} = X~ \ {X}, the strict faces of X, with X~ the closure (all faces including X).

First desideratum: supp X = Sup_{Y in X~} Y°, the supremum taken in the lattice Σ_M, not as a set-theoretic union. Dually, passing to complementary supports: cosupp X = ∩_{Y in X~} ∁_M(Y°).

The next page rewrites this as: Z ∥ X iff Z ∥ Y° for every face Y. The direction ⇒ is trivial. It then compares X° with supp comb(X)° using axioms AtL2 and AtL3.

In classical terms this is the statement that the closure of a stratum is the disjoint union of the open strata of its faces. That holds for stratifications satisfying the frontier condition, e.g. o-minimal cell decompositions or regular CW complexes. Grothendieck wants it as a theorem inside a point-free, support-lattice axiomatics.
errors: The image and transcription write the index of Sup as 'Y ∈ X'; for consistency with the cosupp line and the next page it must be Y ∈ X~, the faces of X including X.

cosupp_M ∂X tacitly presupposes a support attached to the set ∂X of strata, presumably the Sup of their supports. Given the non-distributivity just exhibited, this Sup can be larger than the union, so X° may be smaller than intuition suggests. This is exactly why the desired equality is not automatic, and the page leaves it unproved.

The equality supp X = Sup Y° needs some frontier-type axiom. Without it, the open parts of faces can fail to exhaust the closure. The page only formulates the question, and the next page proves only one direction.

ideas.what: Intrinsic 'open stratum' X° defined lattice-theoretically as supp X ∩ cosupp(∂X)
ideas.modern_name: open stratum / interior of a closed cell; X minus its frontier in a stratified space
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Whitney, Thom, Mather); o-minimal cell decomposition (van den Dries, Knight–Pillay–Steinhorn)
ideas.where_published: Only the programme (tame topology, stratified 'dévissage') appears in Esquisse d'un programme §5–6; the support-lattice formalism is unpublished.

ideas.what: Requirement that the closure of a stratum be the sup of the open strata of its faces, i.e. that P(poset of strata) embeds in the lattice of supports
ideas.modern_name: frontier condition; decomposition of closed cells into open cells; constructible sets as unions of strata
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical stratification theory; o-minimal geometry (van den Dries 1998)

ideas.what: Point-free 'support/cosupport' calculus on stratified figures, with a non-modular lattice of supports Σ_M (from the previous page)
ideas.modern_name: closest: lattices of closed/constructible sets, locales/frames, real spectrum and o-minimal spectrum as point-free models of tame geometry

missed.claim: Grothendieck seeks an axiomatisation of tame stratified geometry in which strata are primary and 'open strata' and 'supports' are derived lattice-theoretically. He asks whether supp X equals the Σ-supremum of the open parts of its faces. The question is posed but only half settled (one inclusion on the next page). The axioms (AtL2, AtL3, ...) remain an unexplored, point-free alternative to o-minimal structures.
missed.quote: On aimerait déjà vérifier que supp X = Sup_Σ Y° ... i.e., passant aux supports complémentaires cosupp X = ∩ ∁_M(Y°)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A strata-first, lattice-theoretic axiomatics of tame topology, where the support lattice is not even modular, differs from both o-minimality (point-set based) and locale theory (distributive frames). It could inform combinatorial or point-free approaches to stratified spaces and exit-path categories. However, it is a fragmentary heuristic set-up rather than a result.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics on the page is the standard 'closure = union of open faces' expectation, recast in Grothendieck's private support/cosupport formalism. The only mildly unusual feature is the point-free, non-distributive lattice setting, which is unpublished but not developed far enough here to constitute a missed result.
transcription_corrections: Index of Sup should read 'Y ∈ X~' (tilde likely omitted or faint); the Σ is a subscript of Sup ('Sup_Σ', with the marginal note 'Sup dans Σ_M').
'une édition[?]' is doubtful; it is likely a technical term of the manuscript (perhaps 'un atlas' or similar). Its reading from the image is uncertain.
The deleted line reads roughly 'Dans le cas où supp_𝔉 F = 𝔉' (deleted).
'où l'on rappelle' is plausibly 'où je rappelle'.
